The rule for each area, with the line that pauses it and the line that resumes it:

- Fundraising: If a raise is in your plan, run the process now rather than waiting. Pause if Risk appetite < 44 or Funding pressure > 76; resume when Risk appetite > 54 and Funding pressure < 66.
- Roadmap: Ship the product bets that move activation or retention first. Pause if Risk appetite < 44 or two weekly readings in a row come in weaker; resume when Risk appetite > 54 and the weekly reading holds or improves.
- New bets: Fund each new bet one stage at a time, and write down what would stop it. Pause if Risk appetite < 44 or Funding pressure > 76; resume when Risk appetite > 54 and Funding pressure < 66.

What it means at your runway:
- Less than 6 months of runway: Cash is what limits you this week, and burn is the lever that moves it fastest. A raise process started this quarter is what lands cash before runway ends. Waiting compresses that margin. A favorable window argues for starting earlier, not later. The hiring pause is what protects the runway every other rule assumes. Reversing it spends that runway.
- 6–12 months of runway: Raise planning has the least slack: if you plan to raise, the process has to finish inside the runway you have, and a favorable window widens it. Each net-new role commits fixed cost against months you cannot extend, so its payback proof carries that weight.
- 12–24 months of runway: You can act on the printed guidance. No emergency cuts are needed while funding pressure stays this side of the pause line. With runway above a year, spare runway goes furthest into the reversible bets the guidance allows.
- More than 24 months of runway: Runway is not what limits you this week. The pause and resume lines are.
